title: One extra offset leaves at least 134 m/s of scatter in five known GJ 163 DRS failures under three weight rules
abstract: We test a constant-offset repair for five known bad GJ 163 DRS velocities in HARPS-RVBank v02. After subtraction of paired SERVAL velocities and a fitted group mean, scatter remains 137.61 m/s. Three controls give 134.64 to 158.72 m/s. Removing any one suspect row leaves 35.58 to 152.90 m/s. The other 198 zero-flag rows have difference scatter of 3.11 m/s. Seven new ESO header checks cover all five suspect exposures and two controls. All five suspect headers have zero target radial velocity; both controls have nonzero settings. This supports a velocity-setting check but does not prove the reduction cause. Earlier campaign work already rejected these five values. The new result tests repair and source metadata. No new planet or independent telescope confirmation is obtained. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and exact external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Aggregate difference scatter, CCF contrast and period scans. One extra constant does not restore metre-per-second agreement.
